item.title: Re: Reality Anchor Story
item.content:encoded:
I'm not sure if this counts as necroposting, but I don't think that Touma would be able to prevent SCP-3922 from entering for numerous reasons.

First of all, when one supernatural phenomena is powered by another, he cannot destroy the secondary supernatural phenomena directly and must instead destroy the primary supernatural phenomena. That's one of the main rules he is bound to. And, since SCP-3922's pataphysical journeys are presumably powered by a device in Corbenic, he would presumably have to touch the device first.

Second of all, I highly doubt that his powers would work on something from a different pataphysical plane than his native one.

That said, I would love to see SCP-3922 get involved in the Sister's Arc. It would be a truly glorious display of justice, and Misaka would get a better ending than what she got in the show.

+ show block
– hide block

However, I have a few questions regarding how SCP-3922 would interact with the native police.

First of all, Anti-Skill. One the one hand, Anti-Skill has some truly dedicated and honorable members such as Yomikawa. Yet, at the same time, it is infested with members of the DA, and it's leadership is corrupt and beholden to the authoritarian leadership of Academy City. So, would SCP-3922 work with Anti-Skill or not? Would it sack the existing leadership of Anti-Skill, purge the DA and then install Yomikawa as a collaborator leader? Would it just purge the entirety of Anti-Skill? Or would it leave Anti-Skill as is?

Second of all, how would SCP-3922 respond to a certain perverted teleporter, aka Shirai Kuroko? On the one hand, Kuroko is an officer of the law who always fights for justice and has many honorable personality traits. On the other hand, she is guilty of many… inappropriate acts towards Misaka, to say the least, and quite a bit of her behavior is probably illegal in Academy City. On the third hand, she is still a minor, so that would also affect SCP-3922's interaction with her. Would they assign her to a psychologist and temporarily suspend her from Judgement? That's probably the most likely respnse.

Honestly, there are so many factors to consider in a potential SCP-3922 intervention in the Index/Railgun/Accelerator franchise that it would probably better as a Tale.

Maybe, just to add some drama to the Tale, it turns out that the Raildex franchise is being used by the Foundation as the subject of a cross-test between SCP-3922 and SCP-826, resulting in a multi-sided conflict involving the establishment of Academy City, Corbenic, and the Foundation.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Reality Anchor Story
item.content:encoded:
Okay, working on an idea for the Certain Magical index world.

+ Idea Below
- Hide

The protagonist is a good guy but his hand is basically a reality anchor and can shatter or negate any supernatural thing from psychic powers to magic. It actually even causes him to have really bad luck and he ends saving people at a cost to himself.
I was thinking of testing the pilot and the three moon guys actually leave him a note telling him, yeah sorry we can’t actually do much. All they manage to do it replace his broken cell phone and debit card. That was all the good they could do, just influence the replacement to get sent out. And wish him luck against the bad stuff that is about to happen. Even the note vanishes when his hand touches it. The rest of the episode goes on the same.
Also, testing a spin-off from that series, A Certain Scientific Railgun. The city that both series take place in is super corrupt. In this one, the protagonist from the series doesn’t show up, for like episodes and rarely. So while we focus on another protagonist the three moon guys show up on mass take over the city, take out the bad guy behind the city and various organizations, stop the experiments on children, and just top-down thing the whole city.
My idea is to show that if a reality anchor isn’t the driving force of the plot the three moon guys can intervene. To show how meta concepts can affect the moon guys. Since this whole thing is a meta to start. What do you guys? I wanted to ask since this would deal with the mechanics of the anomaly.

item.title: A short idea for a possible addition
item.content:encoded:
Subject: Doom Eternal, 2020, M
Interference Point: Scene where Doomslayer lands on Earth for the first time.
Result: Instead of the playable scene where Doomslayer lands alone and can turn to see a gigantic demon in the distance, it becomes a cutscene where 3622-A instances are fighting the giant in airships while two more are attempting to protect civilians. Doomslayer kills the demons, more 3622-A instances landing to help evacuate the civilians, a couple agents, one male, one female, staying to thank the Doomslayer. They turn to see a swarm of demons approaching, Doomslayer pointing to them and saying "Mine." Amused the two agents decide that "Yeah, he's got this" and offer to concentrate on saving civilians while he wipes out the horde. They then give him two special weapons, a 'Triple Moon Special,' an advanced plasma rifle with regenerating ammo, and a special chainsaw that never runs out of fuel. Rest of the game proceeds as normal, save for where the player uses the weapons he got from the 3622-A instances, and occasional references to the Triple Moon group's rescue efforts.

item.title: Re: I have an idea for a new test
item.content:encoded:
OKAY. Maybe these ideas won't be horrible as my last poor attempt. I decided to just focus on the Equestria Girls movies this time.

I also think that maybe a 'banned materials' list would be in order, since past test mention not wanting to give them access to DBZ characters and the like.

Note - The following experiment was performed by using SCP-3922 on the films in chronological order of release, playing each film immediately one after the other.

Subject: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls, 2013, G
Interference Point: When Sunset Shimmer attempts to steal the Element of Magic.

+ show block
– hide block

Result: Sunset is apprehended immediately by pony Triple Moon group members. She is brought before Celestia, who introduces Twilight to her former student. Celestia also explains the Triple Moon group, who approached her not long after Twilight's coronation, Luna and Celestia allowing them to establish a base in Equestria. The first half of the movie consists of Celestia and Sunset, with help from Twilight, working out their differences and eventually reconciling in tearful fashion. In-between scenes of this, there are brief comedic moments of Luna attempting to flirt with the Triple Moon group agents. The second half of the movie has Sunset ask Twilight to come to the school with her to help fix all the friendships she's broken. Sunset meets resistance due to her bullying past, to the point where she is attacked. The attackers are caught by Triple Moon agents, but the damage was done. Sunset's guilt and frustration ends up causing her to change into a different version of her demonic form from the original version of the film, and it takes Twilight and the human versions of her friends to save her. Celestia lectures the school on giving second chances to those who are honestly trying for them, and agrees to let Sunset work off her sins. Sunset is fitted with a monitor bracelet by Triple Moon agents, so they can keep an eye on her, and give her a hoepful speech about turning over a new leaf. New songs, including one sung by the Triple Moon group, replace every musical number.

Subject: My Little Pony: Rainbow Rocks, 2014, G
Interference Point: After Adagio Dazzle notices the column of magic.

+ show block
– hide block

Result: Triple Moon group agents appear from the bushes, apprehending the Dazzlings and crushing their crystals. The Dazzlings are horrified, but the agents promise that they are going to wean them off of their need to feed on conflict. The Dazzlings are carted off, protesting loudly. The majority of the movie focuses on Sunset doing her best to re-earn the trust of the school after confessing her crimes in the last movie, as well as the developing music showcase. A Triple Moon agent now works at the school as a guidance counselor, helping Sunset overcome her lingering guilt. The Dazzlings, all wearing monitor bracelets similar to Sunset, are introduced halfway through the movie. Adagio is having the most trouble adapting, while Sonata and Aria are having a better time of it. Their past as villains gets out, and some of the school starts to turn against them, but Sunset quickly stops it, putting herself at risk to fight off bullies (resembling the Diamond Dog characters in the original show) and saving the Dazzlings. Sunset putting herself at risk earns the Dazzlings' trust, and helps get rid of the lingering distrust in the school. The guidance counselor, satisfied, removes Sunset's monitor bracelet. The Dazzlings are shown starting to realize that there may be something to friendship after all. Sunset is asked to join the Rainbooms as co-lead singer, and while she accepts, she instead opts to sing with the Dazzlings in the musical showcase. The song 'My Past is Not Today' becomes the grand finale, sung by Sunset and the Dazzlings. The movie ends on a hopeful note, Celestia, Luna, and the guidance counselor talking about the potential for good the four of them have.

Subject: My Little Pony: Friendship Games, 2015, G
Interference Point: The scene in Principal Cinch's office, just after 'Sci-Twi,' the human Twilight Sparkle, is threatened to have her Everton recommendation pulled

+ show block
– hide block

Result: A man in a suit and two Triple Moon agents in full gear come in and roughly arrest Principal Cinch, citing her for mental abuse of students, multiple counts of corruption of a minor, instilling improper values in the young, and blackmail. As she's dragged off, the Triple Moon agent in a suit, a woman, says that she's taking over as principal until a proper replacement can be found. She talks politely to Sci-Twi (called such to differentiate her from the pony Twilight Sparkle) about her findings, and gives her a brief lecture on irresponsible magic use. Sci-Twi is even more confused than she was when Cinch was arrested, but the scene cuts away as the agent begins her explanation. The next scene is in the Crystal Prep lecture hall, with the new principal giving a very stern lecture on toxic ambition, how to appreciate your comrades and why its a good thing, as well as bullying, calling out several students on their poor behavior, including the five most prominent Shadowbolts. All five decide to start remedying their behavior by being nice to Sci-Twi, eventually making friends with her. This takes up the first half of the movie. The second half focuses on the Friendship Games, the Dazzlings taking part as members of the Canterlot High team. Sci-Twi ends up making fast friends with the Rainbooms and Sunset, and the rest of the movie focuses on the two schools growing together, Crystal Prep learning how to be good people and Sci-Twi learning about magic.

Subject: My Little Pony: Legends of Everfree, 2016, G
Interference Point: Entire movie

+ show block
– hide block

Result: Using the device on the films in order has drastically changed things. 'Sci-Twi' shows no sign of distress beyond normal anxiety about going on a camping trip, as she has never experienced the Midnight Sparkle entity. In addition, the camping trip is focused on Crystal Prep instead of Canterlot High, with a passing mention of Canterlot High going a couple weeks earlier and having a good time. Cadance is now principal of Crystal Prep. Gloriosa Daisy tries to overwork herself at first, but a Triple Moon group agent confronts her, saying that his group will buy Camp Everfree from them and change absolutely NOTHING about it, even leaving them in charge and funding it forever, in exchange for the magical geodes. The geodes are collected and given to Sci-Twi and the Shadowbolts, who witnessed the exchange. The majority of the movie is a comedic slice of life film focusing on the trip, with some minor wildlife incidents which require the geode-bearers to use their powers to save people. Gloriosa Daisy never becomes Gaia Everfree.
The movie ends with a focus on the Camp Everfree flag, with a Triple Moon flag underneath it, blowing dramatically in the wind.

item.title: Re: I have an idea for a new test
item.content:encoded:
As a general note, it's common courtesy to collapse longer posts for the sake of mobile readers.

I watched FiM until something like three years ago, I think? These names are familiar to me but I have no idea what the actual narratives of the episodes/movies you're altering are. While the entries you're describing may make good crossover fanfics on Fimfiction, they would need to be fundamentally reworked for this log so that they can be comprehensible to an audience unfamiliar with the characters and events you're describing.

A pair of 3922-A agents leap out of a bush and gun down the Dazzlings with plasma weapons, continuing to fire until all three girls are little more than smears on the pavement.

This is disgusting and extremely upsetting to read (I remember liking Sonata…), so if that's what you were going for, cool, but it borders on fetishistic sadism, amplified by the nature of the source material. If you really want to adapt that, it'd need to be a lot more clinical and handled a lot more tactfully.

item.title: A Villainous idea
item.content:encoded:
I got a rough idea for an entry, wanted to see if I could get some feedback.
There is a series called Villainous. It follows a bunch of villains and their boss Black Hat, who is an entity that its an ancient powerful who is often described as the collective evil of the universe. He's an eldritch creature that is a hyper-competent bad guy that could conquer the universe but thought that was too easy and decided to sell stuff to bad guys.
They work at Black Hat Organization; they sell services, weapons, tools, etc., to anyone evil willing to pay their prices of gold, planets, slaves, souls, credit cards. They've been dealing with pretty much every major cartoon network baddy, a few dc comics baddies, and at least one Lovecraftian monster.
As an aside, I got the idea while watching a Livestream of the series creator saying he liked SCP and the stories, even drawing up one of his character Dr. Flug doing a job interview with SCP 049.
My idea is The three moons guys raid their offices. That doesn't go to plan. BHO's vast array of weapons counters every weapon they have. This continues until they bring out the death star they got a while ago to be met by the BH Hat Station. The result they got both blow up, and the three moon guys manage to get in with all the damage.
They drag out the villains but are met with Black Hat himself. They fire their Ace in the hole "Anti-Black Hat" ray, its fire, but battery burns out.
The gunman is revealed to be the real BH; the one they're fired was just a puppet he made look real. The three moon guys try to fight him, but he reveals during the fight he's been sabotaging any weapon that might have hurt him. He let them burn out their last one just to rub it in their faces.
The screen begins to go static as BH starts to grow and transform into something else, something people are better of not seeing.
The screen cuts back to a BH facing the camera to talk to the foundation, much how he does in the show's shorts where he sells stuff to people. In the background, we see his employees gathering the stuff the three moons dropped, ships, guns, corpses. BH may be holding up a copy of the 3922 devices. He chastises the foundation for getting in the way of his work but willing to let that go and offer to make them a deal. Help them deal with Spiegel for an anomaly or two, maybe even take a lizard of their hands.
Maybe have it end with his company logo instead of the usual three moon seal.
The ending feels a bit off, if anyone has an idea, please let me know.

item.title: Addition Idea
item.content:encoded:
I'm thinking of adding an experiment consisting of Valve's "Meet the Team" videos. Here's what I'm thinking:

  • SCP-3922-A Parachute in and arrest Heavy for killing the BLU team without provocation.
  • Soldier is almost immediately arrested for various crimes, and is admitted to a mental institution.
  • All of Engie's Sentries are taken offline by various Electro-Sappers, and SCP-3922-A arrest him for selling equipment to mercenaries.
  • Demoman: Demo is arrested during his interview for public intoxication, and is sentenced to rehab.
  • Scout is arrested for attacking the BLU Heavy, and is also scolded for acting like a child.
  • Sniper is arrested for numerous murders. He is a professional assassin after all.
  • An instance of SCP-3922-A tackles the BLU Scout (actually the RED Spy), reveals his true identity, and allows the BLU Soldier to execute him.
  • After stepping out of his lab, Medic is arrested for numerous crimes, including removing a man's skeleton, practicing medicine without a license, unwilling alterations to humans, etc.
  • Pyro is almost immediately apprehended by SCP-3922-A and admitted to an insane asylum.

Edit: And added. With a few tweaks. Soldier gets arrested for snapping Tom Jones' neck, killing hundreds of German Citizens after WW2 ended, and room-mating with a wizard without a permit. It makes sense in context.

item.title: Pokemon?
item.content:encoded:
I honestly have three ideas:

  • Footage of Pokemon Red, captured from an emulator. The researcher in charge shows his Trainer Card several times, to check his badges (and show Triple-Moon that he's a licensed Pokemon Trainer). Researcher thinks ahead of time, and finishes the game with three specific Pokemon- a Kadabra obtained from the Game Corner (which took hours to get thanks to a rather unlucky spin at the slots), a Haunter from the Pokemon Tower, and the Lapras from the Silph Co. building. He finishes the game by becoming Champion, then catches Mewtwo with the Master Ball. (He reads all of the journal entries on Mewtwo.)
+ show block
– hide block

I expect that the modifications here mostly consist of the replacement of Team Rocket goons with Triple-Moon soldiers, in sprite form, that let the player battle them, while reminding them to stay safe. This causes the following changes:
-In Celadon, the Game Corner doesn't exist. After all, it was owned by Team Rocket. Similarly, the Team Rocket base also doesn't exist. In place of both is the Triple-Moon Research Labs, where Red buys an Abra (which becomes the Kadabra) and a Tactical Ghost-Type Detection Apparatus, which replaces the Silph Scope. Both of them are much cheaper than the large sum of dough the player coughed up in the unaltered version.
-The roads aren't closed- after all, a quick check of the plot reveals that the player NEEDS to get to Saffron City eventually, but Triple-Moon can't allow the player to bribe an officer with a drink! The player still buys a drink, but they instead hand it to a thirsty Triple-Moon soldier, who thanks them for it and reminds them that bribery is a crime. They then check the player's Trainer Card and let them through. (The sprites of the original officers appear behind the soldiers, seemingly tied-up. After all, they *accepted* the bribe, a worse offense.)
-Saffron City seems to be under martial law- the roaming Rocket goons are all replaced by various Triple-Moon soldiers. Silph Co. seems to be just fine- the player instead gets a free Lapras from a Triple-Moon "Plot Contrivance Specialist" (unless someone else can think of a better way to weave it in). Note the lack of a Master Ball.
-The Marowak spirit in Lavender Town isn't angry, for she's not dead. The top floor of the tower contains Mr. Fuji playing with a Cubone and Marowak. Fuji still gives the player the Pokeflute.
-The Mansion isn't burned down, and the Fire Gym is unlocked. A Triple-Moon agent found in the Mansion tells the player that Triple-Moon found illegal genetic experiments being run here, and shut them down. There's no Mewtwo to catch.
-The story ends when the player gets the championship. That, or they sail over to Cerulean Cave, walk to the end, face the screen, and the end slide is shown- again, no Mewtwo to catch.

  • Pokemon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team or Blue Rescue Team, captured the same way as Pokemon Red. Normal playthrough.

The thing about MD:RRT, is that it differs a LOT from other 'humans interacting with another sapient species' stories that have been tested- there's only two humans in the story, the player and a single antagonist that isn't even the biggest problem.

I imagine Triple Moon would do a double-take, seeing as Pokemon Red treated Pokemon as barely sapient but Mystery Dungeon treats them as fully sapient, which recontextualizes the normal Pokemon universe… but their only act here would be arresting Gengar (said antagonist human) before he can send the players off to be exiled.

  • Pokemon White Version, same capture method

And here's the coup de grace. After seeing Mystery Dungeon, I would LOVE to see Triple-Moon's reaction to Black and White, Team Plasma, et cetera. I imagine that either they go full *Little Toaster* and bring about Mystery Dungeon, or they either take the stance of "the Pokemon in this universe are partners" and arrest Team Plasma. Assuming they do the latter…

  • Pokemon Omega Ruby Version, except with a running audio commentary from the player, who goes full Paul. He gets to Mauville and starts IV-breeding and EV-training his Pokemon, spending hours just grinding away until he has a team of Level 100 gods that wipe the floor with anything. Could even have him trade in a Pokemon with Pokerus, to make things faster. Of course, he's constantly both explaining what he's doing and berating his Pokemon. Any Pokemon Amie sessions, if they just consist of the closest the player can get to physically abusing a Pokemon (which is, poking them when/where they don't want to be poked.) Just making absolutely, one-hundred-percent sure to tick off Triple Moon as much as possible.

I fully expect *this* to get Triple Moon to either arrest the player for rampant nonconsensual breeding and slavery of sapient creatures, or full on go *Little Toaster* and wipe out all humans.
